problem_type: Freshness enforcement is bound to a remote name instead of the actual delivery repository
symptom: GH_REPO=a1004657357/Nomi still compares unrelated official origin/main and requests a large upstream integration outside the current PR target; CI=true can also skip the check entirely.
direct_cause: check-fresh-base hardcodes origin/main and returns early on CI=true without resolving target repository identity.
class_root: A freshness baseline must be a fully qualified remote-tracking main tip whose fetch repository matches unambiguous delivery context, followed by an unconditional real ancestry check.
affected_population: Local fork PR worktrees with separate official origin and target fork remotes
Normal same-repository GitHub checkout and ambiguous/missing/misconfigured target contexts
entry_points: check-fresh-base CLI with GH_REPO and optional explicit --remote
GitHub checkout with GITHUB_REPOSITORY and an origin belonging to that repository

external_sources.purpose: Use --is-ancestor on the actual target tip; a common ancestor or matching tree is not the same invariant
Resolve fetch URLs, distinguish push URLs and reject ambiguous multiple fetch repositories
Treat GH_REPO as repository selection context rather than assuming origin owns the target repository

invariants: Only a remote whose fetch GitHub repository matches the target context may supply main
Conflicting repository hints, ambiguous remotes, unsupported identities and missing target refs fail closed
Freshness uses refs/remotes/<selected remote>/main commit ancestry, never an arbitrary BASE_REF, local branch shadow, common ancestor, matching tree or CI flag
No fetch, merge, push, remote configuration, worktree, baseline, workflow, frozen model or product content mutation
Existing preflight/verify-merged command defaults and fetch/receipt behavior remain unchanged

door_reduction.why_not: The existing delivery repository parser/verification and freshness gate remain distinct callers. Freshness now delegates target identity to the delivery owner; the gate stays in place and keeps the strict Git ancestry responsibility. Final doors were regenerated with door-map resolveDeliveryTarget parseGitHubRepository --roots=scripts (2 doors, 3 occurrences); kind=write is the tool classification of parser result assignment, not a Git ref mutation.

generality_proof: The shared delivery resolver binds repository identity before selecting a remote/ref, then the existing gate compares the resulting real main commit to HEAD. Temporary Git repositories exercise true refs/ancestry for origin, fork, newer target main, matching-tree non-ancestors, wrong/missing/ambiguous repos, GitHub-looking relative fetch paths, ref shadows, CI flags and arbitrary environment refs; refs/config/HEAD are checked unchanged after each CLI call. Shorthand normalization applies only to declared repository context, never to fetch URLs.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Resolve one target GitHub fetch repository, matching remote and fully qualified target main commit using the existing URL/parser and Git helpers
Require selected target main to be a real HEAD ancestor, without CI or arbitrary ref bypasses

same_class_entry_points.evidence: An unrelated advanced official origin cannot supply the fork PR baseline or trigger an automatic official merge
Origin still works when it belongs to the declared repository, but CI=true alone never bypasses stale ancestry
Existing explicit remote/base defaults, one-attempt fetch and merged receipt logic are not rewired by this bounded change; only a new read-only resolver is added to the existing owner

recurrence.reason: Any fork/upstream checkout, alias, stale branch or CI environment can otherwise bind a gate to the wrong repository or skip the real ancestry obligation.
same_class_scan: Read check-fresh-base, git-delivery parser/CLI/state/fetch/verification paths and their existing tests
Read workflow GH_REPO=github.repository and fetch-depth=0 configuration without changing it
Observed real fork/main=3d94d96fe and official origin/main=182666a988; original GH_REPO CLI still rejects official ancestry
Temporary real Git tests include wrong repo, missing remote/ref, duplicate aliases, multiple fetch URLs, push-only target identity, qualified ref shadows and untrusted CI/BASE_REF inputs

prevention.invariant: Resolve an unambiguous actual target repository/remote/main before comparing strict main-tip ancestry.
prevention.failure_mode: Resolver errors or missing refs stop the gate; the selected target main must pass Git --is-ancestor with exit 0. No fallback/skip selects an easier commit.
prevention.strategy: Reuse the existing delivery owner/parser and native Git rather than add a parallel target parser or weaken freshness. Keep main fixed in this gate and remove the old origin/CI shortcuts.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove the hardcoded unrelated origin/main baseline and unconditional CI=true early return from the same gate; do not retain a parallel legacy fallback.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No package or Git version is changed. Existing native Git commands and the repository delivery parser own the invariant.

migration: No repository config or stored data migration. Local multi-repository worktrees declare GH_REPO; the existing GitHub repository context selects same-repository origin. Missing tracking refs require the user-owned fetch step, not automatic transport.
residual_risks: A local remote-tracking tip is a cached observation; this read-only gate does not prove it was just fetched. Existing delivery preflight remains the refresh owner
Actual GitHub CI is not executed in this batch; shallow/missing main refs fail explicitly instead of being excused
Default historical-scope root-cause regression is 49/50 with 18 existing removed-path findings; batch-parent-scoped regression is 50/50. No checker, history contract, baseline or ignore is changed
A new A source registration tail remains a separate batch; no unrelated/frozen/working-tree changes are integrated here
